text:
tom: kicking off canary for search-service (change window 16:00-17:30 UTC). toggling feature flag `search_v3` live at 5% for pilot users. release notes: https://redwood.internal/releases/search-v3 :rocket:

deploy-bot: /deploy canary search-service v3.0.0 initiated by @tom. 3 canary nodes up in us-central1. initial ff weight: `search_v3_weight=5`
sara: quick ask 1 1 can we split the 5% to only 'beta' cohort? set `cohort=beta` on canary. keeps traffic clean for QA.
kevin: +1. add circuit-breaker rule: if p99 > 500ms OR 5xx > 0.4% absolute then pause and notify. also prefer soft-fallback path that serves search_v2 for anonymous users.
deploy-bot: updated targeting: `search_v3: weight=5, cohort=beta` -> applied. circuit-breaker rules attached.
pm-bot: release note draft posted and linked to the release doc (internal). cc: support for partner opt-outs.

sre-bot: monitoring hooks enabled: p95/p99, error delta vs baseline, CPU/GPU saturation. automated pause thresholds set.
tom: ramp plan proposal: 5% (10m) -> 20% (20m) -> 50% (30m) -> 100% (1h). add a 20m hold at 50% and require manual ack. objections?
sara: one change: for APAC we keep to 10% max until we validate median latency. region override: `ap-southeast2 max_weight=10`
kevin: add rollback vote channel - if any oncall + PM vote within 15m we execute quick rollback. also script for immediate-patch:
```
# emergency pin to v2
deploy-bot pin search-service v2.9.8 --reason "emergency-rollback" --scope global
```

(8m later)
deploy-bot: canary steady at 5%. metrics: rps 240, p95 95ms, p99 310ms, 5xx 0.08%.
sara: looks good from QA. promoting to 20% now for beta+small cohort. updating flag: `search_v3_weight: 5 -> 20`

tom: remember to flip `telemetry_debug=false` for cohort users to avoid noise in logs.
sre-bot: detected spike: ap-southeast2 p95 increased 40% (from 110ms to 155ms) after the 20% shift. not breaching p99 or 5xx but flagging for review.
sara: holding APAC override. setting ap-southeast2 weight back to 10% and enabling tracing.

kevin: since APAC is flaky, we should enable regional pin that only affects that region if 5xx>0.6% or p99>600ms. script: `deploy-bot pin search-service v2.9.8 --region ap-southeast2 --reason "auto-pin-apac"`

(5m later)
sre-bot: ap-southeast2 5xx climbed to 0.65% over 2m. triggering regional pin now.
deploy-bot: executing: `deploy-bot pin search-service v2.9.8 --region ap-southeast2 --reason "auto-pin-apac"` -> SUCCESS. ap-southeast2 rolled back to v2.9.8. global canary remains at 20% excluding APAC.
tom: good. pausing global ramp until ap-southeast2 traces are reviewed. please dump traces to /runs/6154321987/traces.
sara: traces saved. early cause looks like session-miss storm on our cache layer; adding cache TTL revert in remediation steps.
kevin: starting a slack rollback vote thread in #oncall-ops: `rollback? yes/no` 1 everyone oncall please vote. if 2 yes within 15m we full rollback global.

(12m later)
kevin: rollback-vote tally: 0 yes, 3 no, 2 abstain. decision: continue ramp for non-APAC to 50% with 20m hold.

deploy-bot: queued ramp to 50% for eligible regions. note: `search_v3_weight=20 -> 50` (APAC excluded).

sre-bot: before moving to 50% confirm CPU < 70% and error delta < 0.2% for last 10m.
tom: checks green. proceeding.
sara: reminder to update support doc with opt-out instructions and the temporary regional note.

(after hold)
deploy-bot: 50% reached for eligible regions. hold complete. metrics: p95 110ms, p99 340ms, 5xx 0.09%. no regressions.
kevin: ok to proceed to 100% staggered over 45m. keep APAC pinned until postmortem complete.

pm-bot: published final release note: "v3.0.0 staged rollout; APAC region pinned due to cache TTL regression. Customers in APAC unaffected (served v2.x). Full rollout pending postmortem."
sre-bot: runbook updated with root cause and mitigation checklist. incident severity: sev3. auto-pinning flow exercised.

sara: opening a follow-up EPIC for cache hardening and a work item to add better cohort targeting in flags.
tom: thanks all 1 good teamwork. will close thread once APAC postmortem and we either unpin or rollback. :white_check_mark:
